decisions.decision: D8 - AbortSession() reopens the non-undoable envelope after Rollback(0) rather than being documented as terminal, and refuses (FP_TransactionError) rather than rolling back when undoable=True with a block open
decisions.why: Rollback leaves the FSM in ReadyForBeginTask (UndoStack.cs:724), which ENDS the session envelope, and CloseProject() unconditionally calls EndNonUndoableTask() - so 'terminal' would mean every abort is followed by a broken close, and would make the only revert primitive a one-shot. Reopening makes it non-terminal and safe in an except: block. The undoable=True refusal is because an open unit there is always owned by an UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper whose Dispose() would then raise a second exception out of the with-block exit, masking the caller's original error. Net effect: despite spec.md A3's 'available in both modes', AbortSession is in practice an undoable=False primitive - correct, since per-operation rollback already covers the other mode.
decisions.rejected: Documenting the abort as terminal (breaks CloseProject); rolling back regardless of mode (corrupts the owning helper)

decisions.decision: D9 - use helper.set_RollBack(...), never helper.RollBack = ...; and treat 'a pythonnet attribute assignment that silently succeeds' as proving nothing
decisions.why: RollBack is {private get; set;} and pythonnet synthesizes no property when the getter is private - only set_RollBack exists. helper.RollBack = False does not raise; it lands as a plain Python attribute on the wrapper while the .NET field keeps its ctor default of True, so Dispose() rolled back EVERY UnitOfWork and undoable=True silently discarded every write. Found by A3's live run, fixed at both call sites, verified live (clean exits now commit, raising blocks still roll back). Third instance of the same shape after ILexEtymology.LanguageRA, so it is now a standing rule rather than a one-off note.
decisions.rejected: Keeping the assignment form (silent total data loss in undoable=True); a getattr/hasattr fallback (would re-hide the failure instead of failing loudly)

decisions.decision: Bracket the two lazy-init private helpers (__GetOrCreateChartMarkers, __GetOrCreateDiscourse) inside the helper, not at the call site
decisions.why: Both are invoked before their Create method enters its own _TransactionCM, so a call-site bracket would leave DiscourseDataOA/ChartMarkersOA creation unbracketed; _TransactionCM is nesting-aware so a future caller can still wrap them
decisions.rejected: Bracketing at the Create call sites, or hoisting the helper call inside Create-s existing with-block

decisions.decision: Keep hasattr capability checks and membership tests outside the transaction in AddDependentClause and the two lazy-init guards
decisions.why: A redundant add or an already-initialised slot stays a true no-op instead of opening an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would also Rollback(0)
decisions.rejected: Wrapping the whole conditional including the guard

decisions.decision: For reference setters shaped `if x is None: obj.XRA = None else: x = resolve(...); obj.XRA = x`, hoist the resolution out of both branches so it runs before the transaction opens, leaving a single assignment inside one bracket
decisions.why: Resolution can raise; hoisting it means an unresolvable reference raises without opening an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would Rollback(0). Also collapses two bracket sites into one per method. Applied to the five WfiMorphBundle setters in batch 8; the same shape recurs in Notebook/Grammar/Lexicon
decisions.rejected: Bracketing each assignment separately in its own branch, which opens a transaction after the raising resolve call

decisions.decision: D6 - a mutation deliberately hoisted OUT of a transaction still needs a transaction of its own. AnthropologyOperations.Create keeps its AnthroListOA hoist but gets a separate named bracket ('Create anthropology list'); the `is None` guard stays outside both.
decisions.why: The existing hoist was right about ordering (a missing list must not orphan an ICmAnthroItem) but wrong about coverage: it left list_factory.Create() and the AnthroListOA assignment inside no unit of work at all, which undoable=True rejects outright. Generalises to any future 'resolve before the transaction' hoist - before must mean in an earlier transaction, never in none.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the hoisted mutations unbracketed (illegal under undoable=True), or folding them into the per-item bracket (reintroduces the orphan the hoist exists to prevent)

decisions.decision: For try/except cast sites shaped `try: x = ICast(arg); coll.Add(x) except ...: raise FP_ParameterError`, keep the cast inside the try but move ONLY the mutation into the bracket
decisions.why: Preserves the existing FP_ParameterError mapping exactly while still ensuring an invalid argument raises before any transaction opens. Applied to Person AddPosition/AddResidence/AddLanguage and Anthropology AddText/AddResearcher plus their Remove pairs in batch 9
decisions.rejected: Hoisting the cast out of the try entirely, which would let cast failures propagate as raw AttributeError/InvalidCastException and change the documented exception contract

decisions.decision: Bracket per branch inside each guard for polymorphic Delete dispatch (MorphRuleOperations.Delete's three ClassName branches)
decisions.why: An unmatched ClassName or a missing container must not open an empty named undo entry that Phase 2 would Rollback(0); per-branch labels also keep FLEx undo-menu fidelity (P4)
decisions.rejected: One bracket around the whole if/elif chain, which opens a transaction even when no branch matches

decisions.decision: Keep the dispatch guard INSIDE the bracket where every branch mutates (PhonemeOperations.SetBasicIPASymbol MultiString-vs-scalar, _path_b_attach owner shape)
decisions.why: There is no no-op path to protect, so hoisting the guard buys nothing and would split one logical write into two sites
decisions.rejected: Mechanically applying guards-outside everywhere regardless of whether a no-op path exists

decisions.decision: Treat __WireContext's multi-element path as a single unit of work rather than bracketing each mutation
decisions.why: If IPhSequenceContextFactory is unavailable after members are already added to PhPhonData.ContextsOS, those additions must roll back with it rather than leak into the project-wide owner pool
decisions.rejected: Per-mutation brackets, which would commit the member additions before the sequence create is attempted

decisions.decision: Install pyflexicon editable against the working checkout
decisions.why: FlexToolsMCP loaded flexicon from a copied site-packages install still carrying pre-B1 transaction.py (4 _transaction_depth hits, 0 UndoableUnitOfWorkHelper), so any verification routed through flextools_run_module would have exercised released code, not this branch

decisions.decision: Bracket the deep-copy helpers (LexSenseOperations._deep_copy_sense_to, __copy_sense_content) as ONE unit of work each, not per-field
decisions.why: A failure partway through must not leave the duplicate holding half the source content, or a created sense already in SensesOS with nothing in it. Extends decision 8 (multi-element wiring paths are one unit) from Grammar __WireContext to the Lexicon deep-copy chain
decisions.rejected: Per-field brackets, which would commit each copied property independently and leave a half-populated duplicate behind on failure

decisions.decision: Keep a filesystem side-effect OUTSIDE the bracket: LexSenseOperations.RemovePicture brackets only the PicturesOS.Remove, leaving the optional os.remove of the physical file outside it
decisions.why: The LCM cannot roll back a filesystem unlink. Enclosing it in a named unit of work would imply a reversibility that does not exist, and under Phase 2 a Rollback would restore the LCM reference while the file stayed deleted
decisions.rejected: Wrapping the whole method including the file deletion, which would make the undo entry a lie

decisions.decision: flexicon.CAPABILITIES ships ALL FOUR contract section-3 tokens (ui-injection, refresh-from-disk, per-operation-uow, transaction-rollback), and a token means 'this BUILD implements the capability', not 'the capability is active in your session'
decisions.why: Contract section 3 said transaction-rollback is 'undoable=True only; undoable=False never sets this token', which presumes a mode-aware set; a module-level frozenset cannot vary by mode, and the same tension applies to per-operation-uow which tasks.md mandates B4 ship. Constitution V explicitly permits a mode-dependent guarantee provided the mode dependence is stated plainly in the docstring AND warned once at the boundary where the mode is chosen - A2d's one-shot OpenProject warning already provides the latter, so the mode dependence is now stated in three places (flexicon/__init__.py docstring, contract section 3, OpenProject warning). Withholding a token the build genuinely implements would make the probe under-report, which is the failure mode B4 exists to fix.
decisions.rejected: Shipping only the two unconditional tokens (leaves FlexToolsMCP unable to detect B1+B2 at all - the entire point of B4); adding a mode-aware FLExProject.capabilities accessor (honors section 3's wording exactly but is API surface beyond B4's scope - remains the clean answer if per-session granularity is ever needed, flagged against DEF)

decisions.decision: Describe B4 (and B1) in the contract as LANDED, NOT RELEASED rather than SHIPPED
decisions.why: Contract section 2 line 98 already told FlexToolsMCP to 'treat B1 as PLANNED for integration purposes until it ships in a release'. B4 is on the same branch, and the contract's audience pins pyflexicon>=4.3.0,<5 - a version-pinned install cannot see CAPABILITIES until a release cuts, so calling it shipped would overstate exactly to the reader who most depends on the distinction.
decisions.rejected: Saying 'SHIPPED', which contradicts the framing section 2 already uses for B1 on the same branch

decisions.decision: D10 - a test suite that only asserts the FAILURE path cannot detect a roll-back-everything bug; the commit branch needs the stronger test, and at least one test must survive CloseProject()
decisions.why: Reintroducing D9 turns 19 of DEF-COV's 33 live tests red; the 14 survivors are largely the ones asserting that a rollback happened, which a build that rolls back EVERYTHING satisfies perfectly. That is the shape B1t was mostly built out of. Under undoable=True the commit path carries a silent total-data-loss mode - a discarded write raises nothing and every in-session read still returns the cached value - so an in-memory assertion cannot distinguish 'written' from 'written and then discarded'. Corrected mid-task: the offline suite was expected to stay green under the same mutation and does not (14 fail), because D9's fix had also hardened the doubles; the surviving distinction is that offline guards pin HOW the code calls pythonnet while the live tests observe DATA LOSS.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, recorded not fixed (out of A3 scope): FLExProject.SaveChanges() cannot succeed under undoable=False - i.e. in the DEFAULT write mode. The session envelope holds the FSM in ProcessingDataChanges, but SaveInternal() runs CheckReadyForCommit('Commit at wrong place.') which requires ReadyForBeginTask (UnitOfWorkService.cs:304). Live result is a raw System.InvalidOperationException, and per UndoStack.cs:239-246 that check ROLLS BACK the open bundle before throwing - so the failed save also silently discards the session's uncommitted work. CloseProject() is unaffected (it calls EndNonUndoableTask() first). The mechanism was already documented in spec.md:177, the contract at :149 and cycle2-explore-liblcm-facts.md F4, but nobody had connected it to SaveChanges() being unusable. Pinned by TestSaveChangesIsUnusableInThisMode in tests/operations/test_abort_session_live.py, which asserts the CURRENT broken behaviour and must be inverted when fixed. Likely fix mirrors CloseProject: End/Begin the envelope around usm.Save().

The B2g ratchet has changed character now that the baseline is 0: it is no longer a shrinking countdown but a permanent zero-tolerance guard. Anyone adding a new LCM mutator anywhere under flexicon/code/ will now fail test_no_new_unbracketed_mutations, which is the intended steady state -- these tests are not scaffolding to remove once the feature closes. Contract section 3's original wording for transaction-rollback ('undoable=False never sets this token') is not literally honorable by a module-level frozenset - it presumes a mode-aware capability set. B4 resolves this by redefining a token as a BUILD capability plus documenting mode dependence in three places, which satisfies constitution V. But if a consumer ever needs to ask 'is rollback live in THIS session', the module constant cannot answer it and a mode-aware FLExProject.capabilities accessor would be required. Deliberately NOT built here (out of B4 scope); the natural place to revisit is DEF, which flips the default to undoable=True and largely dissolves the question.

NOT A BLOCKER, but file it: `pytest tests/operations/ -m requires_live_project` stalls indefinitely and must not be used as a gate. ~25 files in that directory (e.g. test_pos_operations.py:487, TestPOSOperationsIntegration.flex_project) define their own fixture calling AllProjectNames()[0] and opening the FIRST REAL PROJECT ON THE MACHINE in place, write-enabled. That is the exact hazard CLAUDE.md warns about. The *_live.py files all use tempdir sandboxes and pass per-file in seconds; the stall is entirely in the older non-sandbox files. Recommended follow-up: migrate those fixtures to target_sandbox. Until then the supported live gate is per-file, never the directory.

DEF's remaining risk is now behavioral, not coverage. Two semantics DEF-COV pinned that callers will hit the moment the default flips: (1) nested blocks JOIN, so an inner block has no independent rollback - catching an inner exception inside an outer block commits the inner's partial writes (test_inner_exception_caught_inside_the_outer_block_still_commits); (2) AbortSession() becomes near-useless in the new default mode - it refuses inside a block (FP_TransactionError) and returns False outside one (D8), so any existing caller relying on it for recovery silently stops being protected. Both are documented in docs/EXCEPTION_HANDLING.md's new 'Atomicity Under undoable=True' section, but (2) in particular deserves a release-note callout, not just a docs section.
